contract: Keep authenticated metadata source identity distinct from executable pip installation input. A pyproject source_path authenticates the plan and is not a requirements projection.
A metadata plan with no requirements_projection remains derivable and source-bound for read-only queries, but cannot materialize or reuse an environment.
Reject missing executable install input before interpreter selection, execution-state allocation, cache access or native commands.

Legacy and governed requirements-source plans retain their existing installation paths and in-memory bounded requirement arguments; metadata plans with a declared projection retain supported behavior.
Use the existing plan installation_path owner and existing typed InterpreterEnvironmentError; no new resolver, receipt, evaluator, CLI or policy exception.
expected_tests: Metadata without projection retains authenticated source_path/source_sha256 and has no executable installation path.
Materialization of metadata without projection raises the existing typed missing-source failure before any runtime selection, allocation or native command; no artifacts created.
Existing positive legacy, recursive governed-source and projected metadata materialization/reuse cases remain in the full consumer module.
forbidden_surfaces: Maintenance owner source or released assets
Loss of metadata/gate source identity binding

source_observation.finding: Metadata source_path addition causes generic installation_path fallback to admit pyproject as an install projection; pip_arguments only rejects after runtime selection/allocation/venv.

verification: Contract and causal tests precede production correction. Pure execution requires a fresh finite admission. No pass or phase closure inferred from source inspection.
